scenes.headline: How a runtime hook stands in for a weight edit
scenes.sub: Refusal-direction ablation on Ternary Bonsai 2 27B, moved to inference.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Pearl! Research found that refusal in chat models runs along one direction in the residual stream. This release acts on it without editing a weight.

scenes.text: Projecting a direction out of a module's output is the same as editing its weights. So do it at run time, and the ternary weights stay untouched.
scenes.say: Projecting a direction out of a module's output equals editing its weights. So do it at run time, and the ternary weights stay untouched.

scenes.title: Same operator, either side of the matmul
scenes.text: (I - r r^T)(W x) = ((I - r r^T) W) x
scenes.say: Why that's allowed: a projection passes straight through a linear map.

parts.note: removes the component along the direction r
parts.say: This term removes the component along r from whatever it multiplies.

parts.note: the module's output: project after the matmul
parts.say: Apply it to the output, after the matmul,

parts.note: the weights: edit before the matmul
parts.say: or to the weights, before it. The result is identical.

scenes.title: Why the edit doesn't fit a ternary model

left.title: Weight edit
items: Three weight levels become a dense float matrix
Storing it means re-quantizing to ternary
That second pass was never trained for
left.say: A weight edit turns three-level weights into a dense matrix. Storing it means re-quantizing, undoing what quantization-aware training bought.

right.title: Runtime hook
items: Wraps each module and projects its output
The packed weights are only ever read
One pack runs with the hook or without
right.say: The hook projects each module's output instead. The packed weights are only read, so one file runs with or without it.

scenes.title: Every write into the residual stream

steps.say: A hook goes on every module that writes the residual stream. The embedding writes it first: that's one.
Each of the sixty-four layers writes twice. First, its attention block's out-projection.
Then its MLP's down-projection. Sixty-four times two, plus one: a hundred and twenty-nine hooks.
The output head only reads the stream, so it isn't wrapped.

scenes.quote: The check establishes that the operator is installed. It cannot establish that the vector points at refusal.
scenes.say: The self-check passes for any vector, even a random one. The paper's other test, adding the vector back so refusal returns, is the half no release repeats.

scenes.text: Where an edit happens is an engineering choice: the math is identical, so pick the side with nothing to re-quantize.

recap: The operator is checked; the vector isn't
scenes.say: To recap: projecting outputs equals editing weights, a hundred and twenty-nine hooks cover every write, and the vector itself goes unchecked.
